title: Dormitory
statementMd:
Student Vasya came to study in Berland State University from the country, so he is living in a dormitory. A semester has $*n*$ days, and in each of those days his parents send him some food. In the morning of the $*i*$-th day he receives $*a*_{*i*}$ kilograms of food that can be eaten on that day and on the next one (then the food goes bad and becomes unfit for consumption).

Every day Vasya eats $*v*$ kilograms of food. It is known that Vasya's parents do not allow him to starve, so there always is enough food for Vasya. Vasya has $*m*$ friends who sometimes live with him. Let's index the friends from 1 to $*m*$. Friend number $*j*$ lives with Vasya from day $*l*_{*j*}$ to day $*r*_{*j*}$, inclusive. Also, the $*j*$-th friend requires $*f*_{*j*}$ kilograms of food per day. Usually Vasya's friends eat in the canteen, but sometimes generous Vasya feeds some of them. Every day Vasya can feed some friends who live with him this day (or may feed nobody).

Every time Vasya feeds his friend, he gives him as much food as the friend needs for the day, and Vasya's popularity rating at the University increases by one. Vasya cannot feed the same friend multiple times in one day. In addition, he knows that eating habits must be regular, so he always eats $*v*$ kilograms of food per day.

Vasya wants so choose whom he will feed each day of the semester to make his rating as high as possible. Originally Vasya's rating is 0 because he is a freshman.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*v*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *v* ≤ 400$). The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 400$), separated by single spaces. Value $*a*_{*i*}$ means that in the morning of the $*i*$-th day $*a*_{*i*}$ kilograms of food come, the food is good for eating on day $*i*$ and/or on day $*i* + 1$ (then the food goes bad). It is guaranteed that if Vasya doesn't feed anyone, there is a way for him to eat so as to consume $*v*$ kilograms of food every day.

The third line contains integer $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *m* ≤ 400$). Each of the following $*m*$ lines describes one Vasya's friend: the $*j*$-th of these lines contains three integers $*l*_{*j*}, *r*_{*j*}, *f*_{*j*}$ ($1 ≤ *l*_{*j*} ≤ *r*_{*j*} ≤ *n*, 1 ≤ *f*_{*j*} ≤ 400$), separated by single spaces.

## Output

In the first line print the highest rating Vasya can reach. In the next $*n*$ lines print, which friends Vasya needs to feed on each day. In the $*i*$-th of these lines first print the number of friends to feed on the $*i*$-th day, and then list the indexes of these friends. Print the friends in these lists in any order. If there are multiple optimal solutions, print any of them.
statementZhMd:
学生 Vasya 从外地来到别尔兰国立大学学习，因此他住在宿舍里。一个学期有 $*n*$ 天，在这些天中，他的父母每天都会给他送来一些食物。第 $*i*$ 天早上，他会收到 $*a*_{*i*}$ 千克食物，这些食物可以在当天和第二天食用（之后食物会变质，无法食用）。

Vasya 每天吃 $*v*$ 千克食物。已知 Vasya 的父母不允许他挨饿，因此 Vasya 始终有足够的食物。他有 $*m*$ 个朋友，这些朋友有时会和他一起住。我们将朋友编号为 1 到 $*m*$。第 $*j*$ 个朋友会从第 $*l*_{*j*}$ 天住到第 $*r*_{*j*}$ 天（包括这两天）。此外，第 $*j*$ 个朋友每天需要 $*f*_{*j*}$ 千克食物。通常 Vasya 的朋友在食堂吃饭，但有时热心的 Vasya 会给其中一些朋友提供食物。每天，Vasya 都可以给当天与他一起居住的一些朋友提供食物（也可以不给任何人提供食物）。

每当 Vasya 给朋友提供食物时，他会给这个朋友当天所需的全部食物，同时 Vasya 在大学里的受欢迎程度会增加 1。Vasya 不能在同一天多次给同一个朋友提供食物。此外，他知道饮食习惯必须保持规律，因此他每天总是吃 $*v*$ 千克食物。

Vasya 希望决定每天给哪些朋友提供食物，使自己在整个学期结束时的受欢迎程度尽可能高。由于他是新生，Vasya 最初的受欢迎程度为 0。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*v*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *v* ≤ 400$）。第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 400$），整数之间以单个空格分隔。$*a*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 天早上送来的食物数量，这些食物可以在第 $*i*$ 天和/或第 $*i* + 1*$ 天食用（之后食物会变质）。保证在不给任何人提供食物的情况下，Vasya 总能找到一种方案，使自己每天都能吃掉 $*v*$ 千克食物。

第三行包含一个整数 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *m* ≤ 400$）。接下来的 $*m*$ 行每行描述 Vasya 的一个朋友：其中第 $*j*$ 行包含三个整数 $*l*_{*j*}, *r*_{*j*}, *f*_{*j*}$（$1 ≤ *l*_{*j*} ≤ *r*_{*j*} ≤ *n*, 1 ≤ *f*_{*j*} ≤ 400$），整数之间以单个空格分隔。

## 输出格式

第一行输出 Vasya 能达到的最高受欢迎程度。接下来的 $*n*$ 行输出 Vasya 每天需要提供食物的朋友。在第 $*i*$ 行中，首先输出第 $*i*$ 天需要提供食物的朋友数量，然后列出这些朋友的编号。每行中的朋友编号可以按任意顺序输出。如果有多个最优方案，输出其中任意一个即可。
